messages.author: b009e0af63bcb5eb
messages.subject: allele coding in a 'wild' family
parts:
Hi, I'm new to QTL mapping and as I'm not working on inbred strains I'm not certain how to code my alleles. I have both parents and a large family of offspring. Some markers have all four alleles (ABxCD) but most have three (ABxAC) or two (AAxAB or ABxAA). I can follow the posted scheme for a 4-way cross for the 4 allele markers, but how would the others fit in?
Thanks in advance for suggestions!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] allele coding in a 'wild' family
parts:
You need to first infer phase/haplotypes and then figure out, for each possible observed offspring genotype, what true genotypes correspond, and then look at the codes in the help file for read.cross, described in the section "Value".

For a marker like ABxAC, we'd have four possible offspring genotypes, and the codes to assign to them would depend on phase in the parents

ABxAC ABxCA BAxAC BAxCA <- parents' phase
AA 1 3 2 4
AB 2 4 1 3
AC 3 1 4 2
BC 4 2 3 1

For a marker like AAxAB, there are two possible offspring genotypes

AAxAB AAxBA ABxAA BAxAA <- parents' phase
AA 7 8 5 6
AB 8 7 6 5


karl

Hey Karl,
From this thread I was able to determine the possible offspring genotypes for parents with phase ABxAA (using your example for AAxAB above).
I also have parents with phase ABxAB and determined the possible offspring genotypes to be:

        ABxAB   ABxBA   BAxAB   BAxBA    <- parents' phase 
   AA      1           3             6            4 
   AB      10         9             9            10 
   BB      4           6             3            1

I just wanted to double check that this is correct because, for example, the AB offspring from ABxAB is technically AD or CB and the numeric coding for 10 from the manual is AD or BC. Just want to make sure that it is OK if the possible genotypes are flipped (BC versus CB). This is true for all the numeric codes from the AB row so I just want to clarify.
Thanks for the help!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: allele coding in a 'wild' family
parts:
I'm not sure what you mean by "am I right here?"

Regarding effect plots: both effectplot() and plotPXG() will attempt to
infer the full genotypes AC,AD,BC,BD in a 4-way cross and will plot the
phenotypes or phenotype averages against those. So even if a given SNP
is not able to distinguish all four genotypes, R/qtl uses surrounding
markers to infer the full information.

karl
